issues.body:
The PR carefully updates every in-app copy surface for the new bzip2 policy — the drawer header comment, WEB_RDF_ACCEPT's comment, DialogPrimitive.Description (line ~452), WebFilePane's paragraph and drop hint (lines ~728/731/767), status-bar.tsx's tooltip, and engine-context.tsx's doc comment — but leaves gui/README.md stale.

gui/README.md:107 still reads: 'On the hosted web target, the drawer parses paste, file uploads, and URL responses in the in-tab WASM engine; compressed uploads and URL responses (`.gz` / `.zip` / `.zst` / `.bz2`) are decoded in the browser before parsing, while HDT remains native-only.'

After this change a `.bz2` upload or URL fetch throws 'Bzip2 archives are supported only by the desktop app.', so that sentence is now false for the exact scenario it describes. (gui/README.md:103's `.gz` / `.bz2` / `.zst` mention is in the NATIVE-loader paragraph and is still correct — leave it alone; import-drawer.tsx:899's native-pane copy is likewise still correct.)

The repo treats user-facing docs that overclaim a capability as a defect rather than cosmetics, and this PR is otherwise an exemplary doc-sync, which makes the one miss stand out.
issues.fix_hint: Edit gui/README.md line 107 to match the new policy, e.g. '...compressed uploads and URL responses (`.gz` / `.zip` / `.zst`) are decoded in the browser before parsing, while bzip2 and HDT remain native-only.' Leave line 103 (the native-loader paragraph) unchanged, since the native path really does stream .bz2. Consider a quick `grep -rn 'bz2\|bzip2' gui/` to confirm no other web-scoped surface still advertises bzip2.
issues.title: Incomplete doc sync: gui/README.md still claims browser bzip2 decode, which this PR removes

issues.body:
The diff adds a real behaviour change beyond the bzip2 removal: IngestedFile gains `effectiveName`, readFilesWithDecompress populates it from decoded.effectiveName, and import-drawer.tsx:270 now calls `guessFormat(file.effectiveName ?? file.name)` instead of `guessFormat(file.name)`. Nothing in the diff fails if that change is reverted.

The new e2e uploads `browser-upload.nt.zst`. rdf-format.ts:28 defines COMPRESSION_EXTS = {gz, bz2, zst, zstd}, so stripCompression('browser-upload.nt.zst') already yields 'browser-upload.nt' and guessFormat returns 'ntriples' from the OUTER name alone. The test therefore validates the zstd decode path (which is valuable) but is blind to the effectiveName wiring — reverting line 270 to `guessFormat(file.name)` leaves it green.

The case the fix actually repairs is ZIP: 'zip' is deliberately absent from COMPRESSION_EXTS, and decompressDatasetBytes returns the zip MEMBER name as innerName. So before this change `bundle.zip` containing `data.nq` produced guessFormat('bundle.zip') -> fallback 'turtle', and the N-Quads member was handed to the Turtle parser. That is precisely the regression `effectiveName` prevents, and it has neither a unit nor an e2e test.
issues.fix_hint: Add a test that goes red without the effectiveName change. Cheapest option is a unit test in gui/app/src/lib/file-decompress.test.ts asserting the zip innerName mapping plus a small pure assertion that guessFormat(result.effectiveName) === 'nquads' while guessFormat('bundle.zip') === 'turtle' — that pins the exact divergence. Alternatively extend the new e2e with a STORED-method zip fixture named e.g. 'browser-upload.zip' whose single member is 'payload.nq', and assert the quad lands in the store; a STORED zip is easy to hand-build (local header + data + central directory + EOCD) without adding a zip encoder dependency.
issues.title: New effectiveName plumbing is untested — the added e2e passes identically without it

issues.body:
The new gate checks only three bytes ('B','Z','h'):

    bytes.length >= 3 && bytes[0] === 0x42 && bytes[1] === 0x5a && bytes[2] === 0x68

Both existing implementations in this repo require the fourth byte to be the bzip2 block-size digit:
  * packages/sparq-client/src/decompress.ts:50-59 — `bytes[3] >= 0x31 && bytes[3] <= 0x39`
  * site/src/lib/rdf-import.ts isBzip2Source — same four-byte test, plus an `application/x-bzip2` Content-Type signal.

The divergence errs in the safe direction (it cannot MISS a real bzip2 stream), so this is not a wrong-answer bug, but it means any payload merely starting with the ASCII bytes 'BZh' is now hard-rejected with a bzip2-specific message instead of falling through to the uncompressed text path. It also means the GUI, the client library, and the site now disagree on what 'is bzip2' means, which is the kind of drift that bites a later refactor.

The Content-Type signal is additionally absent here; for fetchRdfDocument a server sending `Content-Type: application/x-bzip2` is caught by the magic check in practice, so that part is only a consistency point, not a hole.
issues.fix_hint: Tighten the magic test to the four-byte form used elsewhere (`bytes.length >= 4 && ... && bytes[3] >= 0x31 && bytes[3] <= 0x39`). Better still, export the existing detector rather than writing a third copy — either lift site/src/lib/rdf-import.ts's isBzip2Source into @sparq/client next to codecFromMagic and import it here, or reuse CODEC_EXTENSIONS['bz2','bzip2','tbz','tbz2'] instead of re-listing the suffixes inline.
issues.title: bzip2 magic check omits the version-digit byte, diverging from the two existing implementations

issues.body:
The fixture is `new FakeFile('dataset.nt.bz2', [0x42,0x5a,0x68,0x39])` — the name ends in .bz2 AND the bytes carry the BZh magic. isBzip2 is an OR of those two signals, so the assertion still passes if either branch is deleted. The test proves the gate exists but not that both halves of it work, which matters because the extension branch is the one that guards a mislabelled/short payload and the magic branch is the one that guards a renamed archive.

This is not a vacuous test (it does assert a real rejection on the real path, and the error string is pinned), just an under-discriminating one relative to the care taken by the surrounding tests in this file — note the explicit non-vacuity/mutation test at lines 62-77 that this file already models.
issues.fix_hint: Split into two cases: (a) magic-only — FakeFile('dataset.nt', [0x42,0x5a,0x68,0x39]) must reject, proving extension is not required; (b) extension-only — FakeFile('dataset.nt.bz2', <plain UTF-8 N-Triples bytes>) must reject, proving the name signal alone fires. Optionally add a negative guard that a plain file whose bytes start 'BZh' followed by a NON-digit still decodes as text, which pins whichever magic-width decision is made for the issue above.
issues.title: New bzip2 test conflates both detection branches, so it cannot catch the removal of either

issues.body:
WEB_RDF_ACCEPT loses `.tgz` alongside `.bz2`/`.bzip2`, and file-decompress.ts's header comment drops its `.tgz` mention too, but no comment, copy string, or commit message explains it — every other line of the diff is about bzip2.

On the merits removing it is defensible: `@sparq/client` maps `tgz` -> gzip (CODEC_EXTENSIONS) and innerNameForSource returns null for tgz, so decompressing a .tgz yields TAR bytes that the RDF parser rejects anyway. Worth noting the accept list only constrains the file PICKER — handleDrop does no extension filtering, so a dragged .tgz still reaches decompressDatasetBytes and produces a confusing parse error rather than an honest 'tar archives are not supported' message. That drop-path gap pre-dates this PR.
issues.fix_hint: Either restore `.tgz` to keep the diff strictly bzip2-scoped, or keep the removal and add one line to the WEB_RDF_ACCEPT comment saying tar containers (.tgz/.tbz) are not supported because decompression yields a TAR stream, not RDF. If you want the drop path to say so too, that is a separate bead rather than work for this PR.
issues.title: `.tgz` silently dropped from WEB_RDF_ACCEPT, outside the PR's stated bzip2 scope

verdict.summary:
The PR narrows the GUI browser-upload path to gzip/zip/zstd and rejects bzip2 with an explicit desktop-only error, aligning the GUI with the policy the site surface already states (site/src/lib/dataset-archive.ts: 'bzip2 stays out', site/src/lib/rdf-import.ts isBzip2Source). The direction is sound: the early throw in maybeDecompressBytes fires before decompressDatasetBytes, both ingest entry points (file picker handleInputChange and the custom handleDrop) route through readFilesWithDecompress which converts the throw into a per-file `rejected` reason the UI surfaces, and the URL tab surfaces it through finishImport. The e2e zstd fixture is spec-correct (RFC 8878: magic 28 b5 2f fd, descriptor 0x20 = single-segment + 1-byte FCS, 3-byte raw last-block header (len<<3)|1, payload<=255 guarded), so it genuinely forces the lazy fzstd decoder to run rather than mocking it.

Two issues block approval.

(1) Documentation honesty drift: the PR updates the drawer copy, the status-bar tooltip, and engine-context.tsx, but misses gui/README.md:107, which still tells users that web 'compressed uploads and URL responses (.gz / .zip / .zst / .bz2) are decoded in the browser before parsing'. After this change a .bz2 upload throws. The repo's honesty rule makes a stale user-facing claim a real defect, not a nit.

(2) The effectiveName plumbing (file-ingest.ts, readFilesWithDecompress, guessFormat(file.effectiveName ?? file.name)) is a genuine functional fix but has no test that fails without it. The new e2e uses browser-upload.nt.zst, and rdf-format.ts stripCompression already strips .zst, so the e2e passes byte-identically with the old guessFormat(file.name). The case the fix actually repairs is .zip, whose extension is NOT in COMPRESSION_EXTS: guessFormat('bundle.zip') falls back to 'turtle', so a zip holding data.nq was previously mis-parsed. That path remains uncovered.
